degradation.

content.text: Search's client span to geo is about 3 seconds while the rest of the chain is fast, so the wait sits between search and geo. Next I'll check geo's own server spans and the trace structure around that call.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, attr_span_kind kind, span_name, count(*) n, quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6 p50_ms, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, max(duration)/1e6 max_ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('geo','rate','search') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, attr_span_kind, span_name, count(*), quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6, max(duration)/1e6 FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('geo','rate','search') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,1

SELECT time, service_name, attr_span_kind, span_name, duration/1e6 ms, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, trace_id, parent_span_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE trace_id IN (SELECT trace_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='geo' AND duration > 1e9 LIMIT 3) ORDER BY trace_id, time

content.text: Geo's server spans stay fast (about 0.2 ms) while search's client span to geo takes about 3 s, so the extra time is between the two services, not inside geo. I'll check which metrics exist and look at the geo and search pods.

content.text: Rate's CPU time is about 220 in the abnormal period against single digits for other services, which is a large outlier. I'll compare the rate, geo and search CPU and restart metrics across both periods.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, count(*) n, min(value) minv, avg(value) avgv, max(value) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE service_name IN ('rate','geo','search') AND metric IN ('container.cpu.time','k8s.pod.cpu.time') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, count(*), min(value), avg(value), max(value) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE service_name IN ('rate','geo','search') AND metric IN ('container.cpu.time','k8s.pod.cpu.time') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Rate's pod CPU time climbs from about 1.5 to about 220 in the abnormal window, which is a strong saturation signal. Next I'll list the gauge metric names to find CPU usage and throttling series.

input.query: SELECT DISTINCT metric FROM abnormal_metrics

SELECT 'abn' p, metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, count(*) n, avg(value) avgv, max(value) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.cpu.usage','k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime','k8s.container.cpu_limit','k8s.pod.cpu_limit_utilization') AND service_name IN ('rate','geo','search','frontend','reservation','profile','recommendation','user') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, count(*), avg(value), max(value) FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.cpu.usage','k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime','k8s.container.cpu_limit','k8s.pod.cpu_limit_utilization') AND service_name IN ('rate','geo','search','frontend','reservation','profile','recommendation','user') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Rate's pod CPU sits near 1.6 cores against about 0.008 normally, yet its own server spans barely changed. Before going further on rate, I'll check whether search's slow geo calls actually reached geo, by matching client spans to geo server spans via parent_span_id.

input.query: SELECT c.span_name, c.service_name caller, count(*) n, sum(CASE WHEN s.span_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) no_server, quantile_cont(c.duration,0.5)/1e6 client_p50, quantile_cont(s.duration,0.5)/1e6 server_p50, quantile_cont(c.duration,0.95)/1e6 client_p95, avg(c.attr_http_response_content_length) FROM abnormal_traces c LEFT JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id AND s.attr_span_kind='Server' WHERE c.attr_span_kind='Client' AND c.service_name IN ('search','frontend') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC

content.text: Search logs many `results_count=0` responses in the abnormal window, and frontend returns `profiles_returned=0` in the same way. I'll compare search's result counts between the two periods.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, left(message,60) msg, count(*) n FROM abnormal_logs WHERE service_name IN ('search','frontend') AND message LIKE '%results_count%' OR message LIKE '%profiles_returned=0%' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, left(message,60), count(*) FROM normal_logs WHERE service_name IN ('search','frontend') AND (message LIKE '%results_count%' OR message LIKE '%profiles_returned=0%') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,1,3

content.text: Zero-result responses also occur in the normal period, so they are not a clear new signal. Next I'll check whether rate's CPU is pinned at its limit and how search→geo latency varies over the abnormal window.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, min(value) minv, avg(value) avgv, max(value) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.container.cpu_limit','k8s.pod.cpu_limit_utilization','k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime') AND service_name IN ('rate','search','geo','frontend') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2

SELECT floor(epoch(time) - (SELECT min(epoch(time)) FROM abnormal_traces))/30 AS bin30, count(*) n, quantile_cont(CASE WHEN service_name='search' AND span_name='geo.Geo/Nearby' THEN duration END,0.5)/1e6 search_geo_p50, quantile_cont(CASE WHEN service_name='frontend' AND span_name='HTTP /hotels' THEN duration END,0.5)/1e6 hotels_p50, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='rate' AND attr_span_kind='Server' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) rate_srv, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='geo' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) geo_srv, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='search' AND attr_span_kind='Server' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) search_srv FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

content.text: The slow search→geo calls start at the beginning of the abnormal window and most of them never produce a geo server span. Latency of about 1.5 s median and 3 s p95 looks like TCP retransmission, so I'll compare that connection against normal and check the other search and reservation edges.

input.query: SELECT p, c.service_name caller, c.span_name, count(*) n, sum(CASE WHEN s.span_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) no_server, quantile_cont(c.duration,0.5)/1e6 p50_ms, quantile_cont(c.duration,0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, quantile_cont(s.duration,0.5)/1e6 srv_p50 FROM (SELECT 'norm' p, * FROM normal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'abn', * FROM abnormal_traces) c LEFT JOIN (SELECT trace_id tid, span_id, parent_span_id, duration FROM normal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Server' UNION ALL SELECT trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, duration FROM abnormal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Server') s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id AND s.tid = c.trace_id WHERE c.attr_span_kind='Client' AND c.span_name IN ('geo.Geo/Nearby','rate.Rate/GetRates','search.Search/Nearby','reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 3,2,1

content.text: The search→geo edge is the clear outlier: median client time goes from 0.37 ms to 1,577 ms while the geo server stays at about 0.15 ms, so the delay is on the connection itself. The rate pod's CPU jump is the other strong signal, so I'll check its limit and per-minute trend to judge whether it is an independent fault.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, floor(epoch(time)-(SELECT epoch(min(time)) FROM abnormal_metrics))/60 AS minute, avg(value) v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','k8s.container.cpu_limit','k8s.pod.cpu_limit_utilization') AND service_name IN ('rate','search','geo') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2,4

content.text: Rate's container CPU is flat at about 1.70 cores from early in the window, which looks like a pinned limit. To separate network delay from loss on the search→geo edge, I'll histogram the client durations.

input.query: SELECT floor(duration/1e8)/10 AS sec_bin, count(*) n FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='search' AND span_name='geo.Geo/Nearby' AND attr_span_kind='Client' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

content.text: The client durations form a tight cluster around 1.5 s with a tail near 3 s, which fits a fixed added delay on the wire rather than retransmission-style loss. I'll run one check on the evidence queries I plan to cite.

input.query: SELECT p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6 p50_ms, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95_ms FROM (SELECT 'norm' p, * FROM normal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'abn', * FROM abnormal_traces) WHERE (service_name='search' AND span_name IN ('geo.Geo/Nearby','rate.Rate/GetRates')) OR (service_name='rate' AND attr_span_kind='Server') OR (service_name='geo' AND attr_span_kind='Server') OR (service_name='frontend' AND span_name='HTTP /hotels') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY service_name, span_name, p
